question: Why do action and experience vary even when all are equally descents of Rudra?
premises: Even when the status of being a Rudra-descent is the same, action and experience differ.
The body or form of any being is studded with many powers.
This multiplicity of powers belongs to the very constitution of a being.
inference: Differences in action and experience arise because every embodied being is constituted by many distinct powers.
uncertainties: bhāvasya could be read more broadly as 'of existence' rather than 'of a being'.
plain_english: Even when all are equally descents of Rudra, their actions and experiences differ. This is because the form of any being is made up of many different powers.
